question: What cathode does the anode-free full cell use, how is it prepared so that the cell contains no sodium metal on assembly, and what cathode capacity was assumed for its energy density?
expect: pyrite (FeS2), presodiated before assembly (p5.L29-41); Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry, an FeS2 capacity of 335 mAh/g (p5.L52-53)
rendered: The anode-free full cell uses a presodiated pyrite (FeS2) cathode. To prepare the cathode for the anode-free full cell, it is first presodiated, meaning that sodium ions are inserted into the pyrite to create a cathode with a high sodium content. The presodiated pyrite cathode is then paired with a carbon/Al current collector that has been coated with a nucleation layer of carbon and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) to facilitate the in situ plating of sodium metal. The energy density of the anode-free full cell was calculated based on the mass of the presodiated pyrite cathode, assuming a capacity of 335 mAh/g for the pyrite, and the carbon nucleation layer.
